content.title: About
content.content: Rabbit is a lean meat obtained from domestic or wild rabbits. It has a mild flavor, low fat content, and a high protein level, making it a popular choice for healthy diets.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rabbit meat contains fewer calories than beef or pork.
In many cultures rabbit is considered a delicacy and is served on special occasions.
Rabbits grow quickly: they reach market weight in 8‑10 weeks.
Rabbit meat is rich in B‑vitamins, especially B12 and niacin.
In Europe rabbit is often used in traditional dishes such as cacciatore and paella.

items.title: Low Fat Content
items.content: Rabbit meat contains about 5 % fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: High Protein
items.content: 100 g of rabbit provides roughly 21 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑Vitamins
items.content: B12 and niacin help maintain nervous system health and energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of Minerals
items.content: Rabbit supplies phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones and immunity.

items.title: Low Cholesterol
items.content: Compared with many red meats, rabbit has a moderate cholesterol level.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to rabbit meat.

items.title: Bacterial Contamination
items.content: Like any raw meat, rabbit can harbor salmonella or campylobacter if not stored properly.

items.title: Wild Parasites
items.content: Wild rabbits may carry parasites; it is advisable to source meat from reputable suppliers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Rabbit can be roasted, braised, pan‑fried, or steamed. Marinating for a few hours and cooking over low heat helps keep it tender. Popular preparations include rabbit in wine with herbs and garlic, or ground rabbit for patties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh rabbit should be kept in the refrigerator at 0‑2 °C for no more than 2 days. For longer storage freeze it in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Discard any meat with an off‑odor.
